nodes.rationale: Existing graph queries and focused path or explain operations provide scoped architectural context before raw browsing.

nodes.label: Research Before Writing
nodes.rationale: Current official documentation, source, samples, and release notes must be compared before claims or implementations are drafted.

nodes.label: Human-governed Publication
nodes.rationale: Automation may detect drift and prepare draft proposals, but qualification, customer risk, publication, and merge authority remain protected by CI and human review.

nodes.label: Issue-driven Volume Delivery
nodes.rationale: Independent milestones and reviewable chapters make completion measurable and keep broad handbook work bounded.

nodes.label: Sensitive Data Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Customer data, credentials, private architecture, and vulnerability details are excluded from public artifacts to prevent disclosure.

nodes.label: Outcome-led Default Stack Selection

nodes.label: Documented Change Discipline
nodes.rationale: Upstream changes must be summarized without inferring undocumented behavior.

nodes.label: Bounded ADK Author and Independent Reviewer

nodes.label: Exact Reviewed Plan Application
nodes.rationale: The apply job verifies the stored plan checksum and applies the exact artifact produced by the protected plan job.

nodes.label: Separate Plan and Apply Identities
nodes.rationale: Distinct workload identities and protected environments separate planning authority from application authority.

nodes.label: Unsafe Example Rejection Gate
nodes.rationale: Qualification examples intentionally marked unsafe must fail production validation.

nodes.label: Validation and Reversal Criteria
nodes.rationale: Architecture decisions should define tests, metrics, rollout checks, and explicit reversal criteria.

nodes.label: Evidence-Gated Publication
nodes.rationale: Rapidly changing platform and ADK behavior requires claims to be classified and reviewed before prose becomes production guidance.

nodes.label: Approved Chapters Are Production Guidance
nodes.rationale: Existing or technically strong prose remains Draft until it passes the evidence and review policy.

nodes.label: Upstream Re-review Obligation
nodes.rationale: Upstream changes create an explicit obligation to re-review affected guidance.

nodes.label: CI Cannot Replace Engineering Review
nodes.rationale: Automation can detect stale or missing evidence but cannot substitute for engineering judgment.

nodes.label: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Release Notes
nodes.norm_label: gemini enterprise agent platform release notes

nodes.label: Immutable Accepted Decisions
nodes.rationale: Accepted ADRs are changed through superseding decisions, preserving the historical decision record.

nodes.label: External Asset Provenance
nodes.rationale: Every external visual asset must record its license, origin, author, and retrieval date.

nodes.label: Separate Reviewer Agent
nodes.rationale: A separate reviewer provides an independent check on AI-authored candidate changes.

nodes.label: Draft-Only Automation Boundary
nodes.rationale: The maintainer may stage declared files on a draft pull-request branch but never push to main, merge, alter customer cloud state, or accept customer risk.

nodes.label: Validator Completeness Boundary
nodes.rationale: The validator proves that required fields and artifacts are present, not that customer evidence is true.

nodes.label: Customer Data Storage Boundary
nodes.rationale: Real customer records belong in the customer-approved system and confidential information must not be committed to the repository.

nodes.label: Separate Development and Production Targets
nodes.rationale: Development and production use separate Cloud Run targets and should reside in separate governed-cell projects.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Supply Chain Gate
nodes.rationale: A release is rejected unless scanning succeeds, matching build provenance exists, and no High or Critical vulnerability occurrence exists.

nodes.label: Explicit Production Approval
nodes.rationale: Production promotion is a separate customer change-control decision requiring evidence, ownership, and maintenance-window checks.

nodes.label: One Cloud Run Workload per Cloud Deploy Target
nodes.rationale: Cloud Deploy supports only one Cloud Run service, job, or worker pool per target, so additional workloads require additional pipelines.
nodes.norm_label: one cloud run workload per cloud deploy target

nodes.label: Enterprise Agent Platform
nodes.rationale: Separates development, deterministic workflow control, runtime, governance, identity, access, safety, observability, evaluation, release management, and ownership so each agent is not a bespoke application.

nodes.label: Governed Regional Cells
nodes.rationale: Places agent workloads in governed regional cells within the enterprise landing zone to make boundaries, residency, promotion, and ownership explicit.

nodes.label: Volume 3 — ADK 2.x Workflow Engineering for Production Agents
nodes.norm_label: volume 3 — adk 2.x workflow engineering for production agents

nodes.label: Deterministic Shell, Probabilistic Core
nodes.rationale: Uses deterministic code for controls, state transitions, security boundaries, and irreversible actions, while reserving model reasoning for ambiguity.

nodes.label: Runtime Placement Decision
nodes.rationale: Chooses the highest-level managed runtime that satisfies measured region, networking, identity, observability, recovery, support, and workload constraints.

nodes.label: Business-Action Correctness
nodes.rationale: A release is failed if it loses an approval or duplicates a write even when the container remains healthy.

nodes.label: Business-Action Authorization
nodes.rationale: Authorizes the proposed business action at method and parameter level rather than merely permitting access to a tool endpoint.

nodes.label: Multidimensional Agent Reliability
nodes.rationale: Separates entry availability, workflow correctness, side-effect correctness, model quality and safety, customer outcome, and human wait time instead of collapsing health into one metric.

nodes.label: Volatile Fact Freshness
nodes.rationale: High-volatility production facts point to current official pages and require a fresh customer-project observation because terse copied facts become dangerous when stale.

nodes.label: Action and Autonomy Tiering
nodes.rationale: Rates an action by its actual and highest composite effect; material, irreversible, or safety actions are normally prohibited or independently authorized by a qualified owner.

nodes.label: Thin Vertical Slice
nodes.rationale: Proves one governed end-to-end path with real identity, authoritative data, a governed tool, state, telemetry, evaluation, failure handling, and delivery automation before broadening scope.

nodes.label: Customer-Owned Operating Model
nodes.rationale: The FDE must transfer operational authority and design themselves out of the ongoing dependency.

nodes.label: Model Output as Untrusted Input
nodes.rationale: Structured model output must be validated before routing or tool execution, and sensitive data or chain-of-thought must not be logged.

nodes.label: Unknown Write Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: An unknown write outcome enters RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED and is never retried blindly.

nodes.label: Separation of Admission and Apply
nodes.rationale: Admission produces desired state but does not create projects or grant IAM; a separately authorized Terraform workflow performs those actions.

nodes.label: Repository Evaluation Workflow
nodes.source_location: How to evaluate a repository before using it
nodes.rationale: Requires isolated proof, task and failure tests, dependency and data review, measured comparison, a recorded decision, and an exit plan before adopting a repository.

nodes.label: Reproducible, Isolated, Cost-Bounded, Disposable Labs
nodes.rationale: Limits lab risk and makes cleanup exact; a lab demonstrates an exercise but does not establish a product guarantee.

nodes.label: Governed Catalog from Registration to Revocation Lab
nodes.norm_label: governed catalog from registration to revocation lab

nodes.label: Per-Agent Identity and Credential Containment Lab
nodes.norm_label: per-agent identity and credential containment lab

nodes.label: Edge Protection Without Agent Authorization Confusion Lab
nodes.norm_label: edge protection without agent authorization confusion lab

nodes.label: Governed Enterprise Assistant Vertical Slice Lab
nodes.norm_label: governed enterprise assistant vertical slice lab

nodes.label: Approval-bound idempotent workflow
nodes.rationale: Authenticated approval must precede external writes, while a durable business ledger suppresses duplicate work across concurrent invocations.

nodes.label: Reconciliation without duplicate write
nodes.rationale: An unknown outcome after a possible target commit must become RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED and must not trigger a second write.

nodes.label: Runtime placement qualification
nodes.rationale: Placement among Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE must follow measured protocol, latency, concurrency, memory, event, state, location, and maturity requirements.

nodes.label: Defense-in-depth agent security
nodes.rationale: Qualification spans identity, authorization, registry, content safety, egress, target authentication, artifact integrity, telemetry, and incident response because no single control is sufficient.

nodes.label: Synthetic adversarial qualification
nodes.rationale: Adversarial tests use synthetic tenants, records, identities, and secrets and stay within written scope to avoid customer harm.

nodes.label: Workflow-level SRE
nodes.rationale: Reliability is measured from trace to terminal workflow and operation to target, including explicit degradation, capacity, cost, restore, and disaster-recovery behavior.

nodes.label: Evidence-bound reference validation
nodes.rationale: Product claims are decomposed into exact modes and scopes, checked against dated primary Google sources, and separated from customer-selection records.

nodes.label: Unknown over unsupported claims
nodes.rationale: Anything not stated by an official source is recorded as unknown instead of inferred as a product guarantee.

nodes.label: Read-only or draft-only industry thin slice
nodes.norm_label: read-only or draft-only industry thin slice

nodes.label: Prohibited-autonomy rejection
nodes.rationale: A prohibited industry action must be deterministically rejected and visibly routed to a qualified accountable human.

nodes.label: Customer-owned delivery evidence
nodes.rationale: Passing requires customer-owned artifacts and demonstrated competency rather than uniformly green scores.

nodes.label: Bounded draft-only documentation maintainer
nodes.rationale: The maintainer may prepare candidate updates and open a draft PR but cannot merge, accept customer risk, mutate production resources, or write outside its proposal branch.

nodes.label: Retirement completeness
nodes.rationale: An endpoint is not retired merely because it receives no traffic; queued paths, credentials, consumers, state, capacity, documentation, and acceptance must also be closed.

nodes.label: Registry control-plane discovery
nodes.rationale: The catalog proves control-plane discovery, not live invocation health, so runtime health remains a separate signal.

nodes.label: Gateway as authorization service
nodes.rationale: Gateway must be operated as an authorization service rather than a transparent proxy.

nodes.label: Successful authorized outcome SLO
nodes.rationale: Customer SLOs measure successful authorized outcomes rather than proxy 2xx responses alone.

nodes.label: Immediate authorization revocation
nodes.rationale: Google-managed certificate rotation and a 24-hour certificate lifetime do not replace immediate revocation when compromise is suspected.

nodes.label: Bypass-resistant policy attachment
nodes.rationale: Even a strong policy is ineffective if traffic bypasses the protected load balancer or the policy is unattached from the backend.

nodes.label: App as one user-facing service
nodes.rationale: The app, connectors, ACL synchronization, agents, actions, model, and feature settings are operated as one service because failures across them affect one user journey.

nodes.label: Behavioral recovery proof
nodes.rationale: Recovery is demonstrated by ACL, relevance, citation, safety, and action tests rather than a green user interface.

nodes.label: Business-journey SLOs
nodes.rationale: Customer objectives must derive from the business journey; policy denials are not availability failures, while dependency failures are counted according to the customer dependency model.

nodes.label: Narrow platform containment
nodes.rationale: Containment selects the affected ingress, revision, policy, identity, storage behavior, or preview dependency without weakening IAP or granting public access.

nodes.label: Privacy-preserving query catalogue
nodes.rationale: Operational queries correlate structured identifiers while excluding raw identity and request content from logs.

nodes.label: Correlation is not proof
nodes.rationale: Correlated revision, request, rollout, image, and trace identifiers support diagnosis but do not by themselves prove policy correctness or write ordering.

nodes.label: Governed business workflow
nodes.rationale: The ADK workflow is operated as a governed business system with business, workflow, approval, operation, release, and trace keys rather than merely as a model endpoint.

nodes.label: Narrowest rehearsed kill switch
nodes.rationale: Containment should disable the smallest affected tool, action, tenant, or invocation path while preserving safe read-only operation where possible.

nodes.label: Reconcile before retry
nodes.rationale: A timeout is not a confirmed failure; every unknown write is reconciled against the target operation ID before any retry.

nodes.label: Structured redacted telemetry
nodes.rationale: Debugging uses approved structured fields without weakening redaction or adding raw request or model content.

nodes.label: Revision-aware runtime containment
nodes.rationale: Containment freezes promotion and routes work to a qualified revision or manual process, while acknowledging that traffic rollback does not reverse business side effects.

nodes.label: Separate-state runtime recovery
nodes.rationale: Artifacts, configuration, policy, identity, sessions, queues, and business ledgers have separate recovery objectives and must be restored accordingly.

nodes.label: Normalized-action security operations
nodes.rationale: Security operations begin from the normalized business action and its full decision chain; raw prompt capture is not automatically required or approved.

nodes.label: Narrow security containment
nodes.rationale: Contain the smallest affected action, route, identity, tool, secret, release, or tenant instead of broadly shutting down the project when narrower containment is safe.

nodes.label: Content Inspection Is Not Business Authorization

nodes.norm_label: platform signal and business evidence gap

nodes.label: Catalog Is Not Endpoint Health Evidence
nodes.norm_label: catalog is not endpoint health evidence

nodes.label: Measurable Engagement Outcome
nodes.rationale: An engagement should define workflow, population, baseline, target, guardrails, and a stop or retire condition.

nodes.label: Customer Confidentiality Boundary
nodes.rationale: Customer names, content, credentials, traces, network details, personal data, and regulated information are excluded unless an authorized process permits them.

nodes.label: Evidence-Based Advancement
nodes.rationale: Every maturity level requires exit criteria, an accountable owner, evidence, residual risks, and an explicit advance, remain, constrain, or stop decision.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Publication
nodes.rationale: Local tests do not prove a customer deployment, unresolved risks must remain visible, and agent verdicts cannot satisfy customer risk acceptance.

nodes.label: Real Environment Evidence
nodes.rationale: Customer qualification evidence must identify the real environment and executor; examples and generated records cannot be treated as passed customer qualification.

nodes.label: Official Source Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Research prioritizes official product documentation and release notes, then pinned source, samples, architecture guidance, and official practice material.

nodes.label: Research Stop Conditions
nodes.rationale: Research stops when material official support or maturity status is unavailable, or when product documentation conflicts with source code.

nodes.label: Vendor Claim Boundary
nodes.rationale: OpenAI and Anthropic evidence can inform comparison but cannot establish a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform product contract.

nodes.label: Authority Non-Expansion
nodes.rationale: Permissions, customer authority, regions, and maturity must not be broadened merely to make an example pass.

nodes.label: Documentation-Only Justification
nodes.rationale: Documentation-only is valid only when an impact manifest explains why implementation, infrastructure, tests, labs, and operations remain correct.

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Documentation Role
nodes.rationale: The documentation workflow uses a separate project and a custom role containing only prediction and service-usage permissions.

nodes.label: Cloud Armor Policy Attachment Boundary
nodes.rationale: The module creates but does not attach the policy; the load-balancer stack must attach it, enable logging, and verify attachment and direct-origin controls.

nodes.label: Terraform Bootstrap Dependency Boundary
nodes.rationale: State, identity, initial deployment identities, and first federation bindings must be bootstrapped outside the unapplied stack to avoid circular dependencies.

nodes.label: Separate Plan and Apply Federation Pools
nodes.rationale: Separate pools prevent a token admitted for planning from impersonating the apply identity.
nodes.norm_label: separate plan and apply federation pools

nodes.label: Preview Customer Exception
nodes.rationale: Preview Agent Registry, Gateway, and Identity capabilities require explicit customer exceptions and rollback agreements.

nodes.label: Dry-Run Audit Mode
nodes.rationale: DRY_RUN maps to audit-only fail-open behavior and must never be promoted to production, while ENFORCED is fail-closed.

nodes.label: Empty OAuth Scope Rejection
nodes.rationale: An empty scope allowlist is rejected because Google interprets it as all scopes.

nodes.label: Agent MCP Server and HTTPS Endpoint Registrations
nodes.norm_label: agent mcp server and https endpoint registrations

nodes.label: Registry Input Validation
nodes.rationale: Insecure URLs, invalid kind/spec/protocol combinations, and unsupported us/eu endpoint-binding combinations are rejected before deployment.

nodes.label: Registration Assurance Boundary
nodes.rationale: Catalog registration alone does not establish endpoint health or Gateway authorization.

nodes.label: Semantic Review of Agent Metadata
nodes.rationale: Agent Cards and tool specifications are production metadata and therefore require semantic review before apply.

nodes.label: Default-deny WAF Source CEL Rate-limit and Threat Intelligence Rules
nodes.norm_label: default-deny waf source cel rate-limit and threat intelligence rules

nodes.label: Preview and Enforcement Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Rules remain in preview until sampled logs and false positives are inspected, exclusions are narrowly tuned, and change approval is obtained.

nodes.label: Adaptive Protection Detection Without Automatic Deployment
nodes.rationale: Adaptive Protection findings are detected without automatically deploying a policy response.
nodes.norm_label: adaptive protection detection without automatic deployment

nodes.label: Backend Attachment and Logging Handoff
nodes.rationale: The consuming load-balancer stack owns backend services and must attach the policy to every internet-facing backend, enable logging, and verify the handoff through a customer-environment integration test.

nodes.label: Managed Protection Plus Subscription Prerequisite
nodes.rationale: Threat Intelligence feeds may require Managed Protection Plus, so the customer subscription must be confirmed before those feeds are enabled.

nodes.label: Enterprise Search Datastore and LLM Add-on
nodes.norm_label: enterprise search datastore and llm add-on

nodes.label: CMEK Creation Order and Location Guardrail
nodes.rationale: CMEK service-agent grants and registration occur before data creation, and CMEK is rejected in global because that location does not support it.
nodes.norm_label: cmek creation order and location guardrail

nodes.label: App-scoped End-user IAM
nodes.rationale: Users receive roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser only on the app; project-wide and broad public principal grants are excluded.

nodes.label: Gemini Enterprise Observability Handoff
nodes.rationale: Provider 7.42.0 lacks a first-class observability resource, so operators must use the supported API or console, retain the change record, and validate telemetry before go-live.
